issues.title: Exact-bitmap join filter through CM integral compress projections (offset-shifted, no hashed BF)
issues.hypothesis: Hot JSON profile of q09.m0 (505ms wall, ~3.4s CPU): HASH_JOIN o_orderkey=l_orderkey costs 1.39s CPU, the biggest operator (lineitem scan 0.77, lineitem HJ 0.51, agg 0.20). Its build side is 3.27M rows, so the pointer table is ~8M entries / 64MB. The probe side is all 15M orders rows, because the orders scan gets NO dynamic filter: scan -> PROJECTION(__internal_compress_integral_uinteger(o_orderkey,1)) -> HJ, and PushdownJoinFilterExpression (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:23) only passes colrefs and integral casts. About 80% of those probes miss, and each miss is a random cache miss into the 64MB table. E0003 already pushed min/max plus a HASHED BF through the compress projection. The orders rows fell 15M->2.96M, but bench was +4.7% (local -8.2%), because hashing 15M keys and doing random lookups into a ~5MB hashed BF cost about what it saved. What is different now: E0004 added exact-bitmap mode. Here the build keys span about 60M values with 3.27M keys, about 18 bits/key, under the 128 cap and under 2^31. So the orders scan filter becomes: subtract a constant, then do one bit test. There is no hashing, and because the probe-side keys arrive clustered or sorted (PK order), the walk through the 7.5MB bitmap is nearly sequential. It is also exact, so the HJ receives exactly the 3.27M matching rows.
issues.plan: 1) Optimizer: in PushdownJoinFilterExpression (src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:23), accept a BOUND_FUNCTION whose name starts with __internal_compress_integral_ (see src/function/scalar/compressed_materialization/). Conditions: child 1 is a non-NULL constant castable to BIGINT, and child 0 is integral, at most 64 bits, and not UBIGINT. Recurse into child 0, then record `Value offset` on JoinFilterPushdownColumn (src/include/duckdb/execution/operator/join/join_filter_pushdown.hpp), and copy it wherever columns are rewritten (UNION children). TopN and RowGroupPruner also call GetPushdownFilterTargets: they must bail out when a target has an offset. 2) In JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp:870), when an offset is present: cast min/max to HUGEINT, add the offset, then cast to storage_type (skip the column if a cast fails); skip the IN filter. Compute has_cast against the decompressed storage type, so it does not by itself block the BF. 3) BF only in exact mode when there is an offset. Call TrySetExactBloomFilterRange (:845) with the build-side compressed min/max, unchanged. Its build_type==probe_type check must be relaxed for the offset case, because probe storage is BIGINT and the build is UINTEGER. If the HT BloomFilter is not exact after that call, do NOT push a hashed BF for an offset column (min/max only). 4) BFTableFilter (src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp plus its header): add an int64 key_offset/has_key_offset and serialize it as optional fields. In exact-mode Filter/FilterValue/CheckStatistics, test bit ((v - key_offset) - min) on the probe vector's own physical type. The existing out-of-range rejection must happen after the shift. If has_key_offset is set and the filter is not exact, the probe must never run (assert). 5) PushBloomFilter (:788) passes the offset of the pushdown column. Test: compare joins on real tables against `+0` versions (no pushdown), for example a count/sum of orders⋈lineitem with a lineitem-side filter. Confirm with EXPLAIN ANALYZE that the orders scan shows `IN BF` and that its cardinality drops.
issues.expected_gain: q09: orders HJ 1.39s CPU -> ~0.5-0.7s, orders scan +~0.05s, so about -12..-20% wall. If bench shows <5%, the orders HJ is build-dominated (3.27M random inserts), and the next step would target the build rather than the probe.
issues.generality: Any hash join whose probe-side integer key is CM-compressed before the join (common: CM compresses integer keys with known stats on both sides) and whose build keys are dense enough for the exact bitmap. Typical case: PK/FK joins where the fact-derived side is the build and the dimension or PK table is the probe. A query could get slower if the bitmap filter passes almost everything; SelectivityOptionalFilter pauses it then. Hashed BF behaviour is unchanged.
issues.risk: Medium. The offset arithmetic must match the CM projection exactly: probe value v maps to (v - offset) and must equal the build's compressed key. Using the wrong offset or the wrong sign gives wrong results, so test with keys whose min is non-zero. TopN and RowGroupPruner must reject offset targets. Use only the probe-side offset from the compress expression on that side.

output.memory:
# Memory (db_evolve, q09 specialisation run)

## Status: gen1 r5, best 2.266x (E0001 contains sel -29%, E0002 BF first key multi-key HJ -22%, E0004 exact bitmap BF -20%)
- E0003 (offset-aware min/max + HASHED BF through CM compress) RETIRED: bench +4.7% (local -8.2%); orders 15M->2.96M rows
  but HJ only 2.22->1.88s (cold profile). Bad implementation choice (hashing 15M keys into random 5MB BF), not a dead idea.
- r5 dispatched: same pushdown but EXACT bitmap only (offset-shifted bit test, no hashing; orders PK-sorted -> sequential).
  If this also gives <5%: orders HJ is build-dominated (3.27M random inserts into 64MB pointer table) -> target build next.

## q09 HOT profile (r5, JSON profiling in one dbe-tool sql call, 505ms wall, ~3.4s CPU)
- HJ o_orderkey=l_orderkey 1.39s (build 3.27M from lineitem side, probe 15M orders, NO filter on orders scan: CM compress proj blocks)
- lineitem scan 0.77s (60M -> 3.27M exact via bitmap on l_partkey); lineitem⋈(part⋈ps) HJ 0.51s
- HASH_GROUP_BY 0.20s (175 groups, keys = compressed n_name uhugeint + utinyint year); compress proj before agg 0.10s
- part scan (contains) 0.17s; orders scan 0.06s; partsupp scan 0.04s; rest tiny.
- Cold `dbe-tool profile` numbers are ~2x inflated & distort shares (scan looked 4.2s); use hot JSON trick below.
- Hot micro: lineitem count(*) WHERE l_partkey%20=3 ~55ms wall; + selecting 5 more bitpacked cols at 5% -> ~175ms.
  All 6 lineitem cols are BitPacking.

## Remaining ideas
- Agg 0.20s+0.10s proj for 175 groups over 3.27M rows: ~90ns/row, slow for a tiny group count. Maybe skip string CM compress
  before agg with tiny group counts, or a perfect/small-group agg path. Not investigated in code yet.
- lineitem⋈ps HJ 0.51s (2 keys, build 436K): maybe fine.
- Orders HJ build cost if r5 shows probe isn't dominant.
- Sibling: sparse-select decode tweaks on bitpacked scan gave 0% (Bitpacking select no gain).

## Codebase facts
- JSON profile trick (hot): one dbe-tool sql call: PRAGMA enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='/tmp/x.json';
  run query twice; PRAGMA disable_profiling; SELECT unnest(regexp_extract_all(regexp_replace(content,'\s+',' ','g'),
  '"operator_timing": [0-9.e-]+|"operator_name": "[A-Z_ ]+"|"operator_cardinality": [0-9]+',0)) FROM read_text('/tmp/x.json')
- dbe-tool: no shell variables (B=... blocked); pipes to grep/tail work. Each sql call is a fresh process (first query cold).
- Optimizer order: STATISTICS_PROPAGATION (adds CM compress projections) runs BEFORE JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN.
  PushdownJoinFilterExpression (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:23) passes only colref and integral casts.
- TopN optimizer and RowGroupPruner reuse GetPushdownFilterTargets: any value-transforming pass-through must be rejected there.
- FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp:870): min/max -> SelectivityOptionalFilter, IN for small HTs, BF only if !has_cast &&
  first key && CanUseBloomFilter (:761). Deferred BF push at HT finalize (:588 PushBloomFilter :788).
  TrySetExactBloomFilterRange (:845): exact bitmap if same physical type, range<2^31, <=128 bits/key.
- RowGroup::Scan (row_group.cpp:694): filter cols via Filter() in adaptive order, others via Select(sel). Top-level OPTIONAL_FILTER
  set always-true at zonemap check; AND-of-optionals is not (q19 sibling: skipping it gave 0%).
- BF (planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp): hashed 12 bits/key; exact mode via SetKeyRange (E0004). Insert in JoinHashTable::InsertHashes.
- Hash<uint32>(c) == Hash<int64>(k) for 0<=v<2^32 (hash.hpp:36-60).
- Testing tip: range()/CTE sources don't get pushed filters; use real tables vs `col+0` keys to block pushdown.
- Adding `hash(o_orderkey)%50=0` to q09 flips orders to build side -> not usable to isolate HJ build cost.

## Exhausted / retired
- Multi-key BF: DONE (E0002). contains selectivity: DONE (E0001). Exact bitmap BF: DONE (E0004).
- Hashed BF through CM offset: retired E0003 (+4.7%); exact-only variant is r5.
